list: The official 55 trophies (1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden), as PlayStation publishes them and as Exophase and PSNProfiles listed them before this guide was built.
rarityNote: Rarity is the share of tracked players who had earned the trophy in Exophase's launch recording of the game's trophy page (19 November 2026, 638 players tracked). It is a launch-week snapshot, not a live figure: story trophies read low because few tracked players had finished the campaign, and the opening mission reads 100% because every tracked player had completed it.

sources.psn: PlayStation — the official Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list: names, descriptions and grades as published (mirrored in the dataset this guide ships with)
sources.exophase: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI (PSN) trophies, hidden flags and recorded rarity: https://www.exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/
sources.psnprofiles: PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list and community guide notes: https://psnprofiles.com/trophies/

roadmap.title: Story first, eyes open
roadmap.text: Play the story from Gone Fishing to the final mission. Every chapter and named-mission trophy (ids 2-13) pops on completion and none can be missed. Two things need attention while you are here: make the unscheduled VCIA departure (Catch Me If You Can) during the story's VCIA visit, and keep a manual save before story choices so Actions Speak Louder can be revisited. If a one-shot set-piece goes perfectly, remember Bad Luck, I Guess asks for a second try.

roadmap.title: Finish every strand
roadmap.text: Close out the stranger strands: the final missions for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone, plus Bret's unique-animal hunt. Five strand finales and the hunt feed directly into Strangers & Freaks, which needs 8 completed strands, so nothing here is wasted time. Doing this before the endgame keeps every strand available regardless of how the story lands.

roadmap.title: The Leonida collection
roadmap.text: Sweep the collectible layer of the map: 3 Collectible Card sets, WAiNK It at 100 locations, all 18 meditation spots, all 52 areas of Leonida, and 100 discovered vehicles. Use this tracker's counters as you roam — a location is cheapest to log the first time you pass it, and the exploration trophy completes naturally while you sweep the rest.

roadmap.title: Activities and mastery
roadmap.text: Work the activity board: gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, 250 stunts, a Top Fun drone-race win at all 14 locations, 20 different race wins, 50 challenges, one try of each of the 9 activity types, Cal's fishing challenge and one finished arcade game. The Shootist is the phase's long pole — practise each range weapon class early instead of grinding it at the end.

roadmap.title: Crime, money and the open world
roadmap.text: Everything the open world still owes you: the robbery set (jewelry store undetected, 5 bank vaults, an armored truck, one illegal operation per gang, 3 shops back-to-back with your partner), losing a 4-star wanted level with your partner, laundering $250,000 of Marked Bills, spending $100,000, all 8 garages, 10 Scooter Bros registrations, and the one-off moments — the showroom escape, the bowling alley, the Ocean Beach cocktail, a Rhino, a 5-kill Combat Focus and whatever the strange event turns out to be.

roadmap.title: 100% and the platinum
roadmap.text: When the tracker shows every other trophy earned or counted out, close A Long Road by attaining 100% completion — its checklist is the sum of the phases above — and Vice Got a Price!, the platinum, follows automatically once the other 54 are yours.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum: it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, with nothing extra to do. Plan backwards from it — the two golds (the final mission and 100% completion) are the long poles, and every other trophy on this list feeds one of them. If the platinum does not pop, sort the tracker by Not earned: the straggler is almost always a counted trophy whose counter is a few short.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story-locked and unmissable: finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission, and the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen. Exophase's launch recording shows it at 100% because every tracked player in that early cohort had already finished the opener. Nothing to prepare — just start the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete the last mission of Chapter 1 and the trophy is yours. Chapter trophies cannot be skipped or failed permanently — a failed mission simply retries — so no save management is needed this early.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 2. The name is censored on PlayStation itself, asterisks included — it is not a typo in this guide. Keep playing the gold story markers; the trophy pops when the chapter closes.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete Chapter 3. By now the map and activity board are opening up; resist the full collectible sweep until the story is done — the roadmap's later phases assume free roam with everything unlocked.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete Chapter 4. This is a good point to bank a manual save — the choice-driven trophy Actions Speak Louder is tracked from here on, and a pre-choice save is the cheapest insurance on the whole list.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The story gold: complete the final mission. It cannot be missed — the campaign funnels you here — but go in stocked: full health, armour and ammo, and your best weapons upgraded, because the finale is the campaign's longest fight. Earning it also closes the story arc the roadmap's cleanup phases build on.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete the story mission Breakfast Run when it appears on the map. Named-mission trophies like this one pop on the mission-complete screen; if you fail a section, the retry keeps all progress toward it.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete The Cartel Heist, the story's set-piece robbery. Heist missions reward a loud-or-quiet choice in setup; either route earns the trophy, so pick the approach your loadout suits. It is also good practice for the free-roam robbery trophies in phase 5 of the roadmap.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete the story mission Child's Play. Like the other named-mission bronzes it is awarded for completion alone — no medal, timer or no-death condition is attached to it.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete the story mission Headliners. Just follow the story markers; the trophy pops when the mission wraps, whatever route you took through it.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete VCIA Takedown. Remember this visit to the VCIA airport — the missable trophy Catch Me If You Can is earned by leaving this same airport in an unscheduled way, and the story visit is the guaranteed chance to do it. See that trophy's guide before you finish here.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Unmissable: complete Operation Savage Glory. A combat-heavy mission — bring armour and a full special-ability meter. Completion is the only condition.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The completion gold: reach 100% on the game's own completion checklist — story, strands, collectibles, activities and world events all feed it. Work the roadmap phases in order and use this tracker as the mirror of the in-game percentage; when the game says 99%, the missing line is usually a partially counted set (cards, spots or challenges), so sort by counter progress and finish the closest set first.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunt events across Leonida — jumps, near-miss chains and the other stunt categories the game tracks. They are scattered everywhere, so log them opportunistically: when a stunt icon appears on a route you are already driving, take the detour. Use the counter on this card to pace the grind; saving all 250 for the cleanup phase is the slowest way to earn it.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the game's 9 activity types once — you only have to start each one, not master it. This is the cheapest bronze on the list and the natural first stop of the activity phase: one pass over the activity board unlocks it and shows you which activities the harder trophies (races, ranges, fishing) will ask more of.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the list's main skill gate: learn each weapon class's rhythm on its early challenges, prioritise accuracy streaks over raw speed, and replay a challenge immediately while its target pattern is fresh. Spread the work across the playthrough — a few golds per session — instead of leaving 42 for the endgame.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations — a finish is not enough, the trophy needs the win at every site. Learn each course with one slow reconnaissance run, then attack it: drone races are won on the racing line through the gates, not on top speed. Tick each location off in the counter as you win it.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — repeats of the same race do not stack, so breadth beats grinding one easy circuit. Bring a tuned car in its class, learn the first two corners of each course (where the AI packs tightest), and move on as soon as a race is won; the counter here tracks distinct wins.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is one of the stranger-strand characters, so this unlocks as his strand opens; the challenge is a head-to-head catch contest, won by landing fish steadily rather than chasing one big catch. It carries the highest recorded rarity on the list in Exophase's launch snapshot (2.04%) simply because fishing is easy to walk past — do not walk past it.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish, at any arcade cabinet. Pick the shortest cabinet game you find and see it through to its end screen — starting games does not count, finishing one does. Pairs naturally with Master of None, since an arcade visit is one of the 9 activity types.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's mission strand through to his final mission. Stranger strands unlock in stages as the story advances; work each new stage as it appears so the finale is ready when you are. This finale is one of the 8 strands Strangers & Freaks counts, and finishing strands before the endgame is the roadmap's insurance policy.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's mission strand through to his final mission. Same rhythm as the other strand finales: clear each stage as the story unlocks it, and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks. If a stage seems missing, progress the main story — strand stages are chapter-gated.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's mission strand through to his final mission. Keep Billy's stages moving alongside the campaign; his finale is one of the 8 strands needed for Strangers & Freaks, and strand finales are quick once unlocked.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. The five named finales in this guide — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — are five of them; Bret's hunt and Cal's fishing strand are on the same board. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so half-finished strands are the usual reason this silver lags: finish strands, do not just start them.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's mission strand through to his final mission. Work the stages as they unlock during the campaign; the finale counts toward Strangers & Freaks like the other named strands.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's mission strand through to his final mission. If Tyrone's next stage is not on the map, advance the story a chapter and check again — strand availability follows campaign progress.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. The spots sit in scenic, out-of-the-way places, so this pairs with the exploration sweep for The Goodtime State: log each spot the first time you pass it and let the counter here track the set. A spot only counts once you complete the meditation interaction, not by standing on it.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret sends you after. This is a strand task for Bret: take his hunt when it opens, track the animal in its territory, and bring the hunt home to finish it. It sits in the roadmap's strand phase alongside the five named finales.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. Cards are found across Leonida and grouped into sets, so collect in sweeps by area rather than hunting single cards, and finish one set completely before spreading to the next — the trophy counts completed sets, not cards held. The last card of a set is always the bottleneck; clear its area methodically.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 different locations. Like the other hundred-count trophies, this is won by habit, not by a single grind: trigger it whenever you arrive somewhere new and let the counter accumulate through the whole playthrough. Saving it for cleanup means 100 deliberate stops; weaving it into every phase makes it nearly free.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges. Challenges surface through play — driving, combat, activities — so check the challenge board whenever you are between missions and knock out the nearly-done ones first. Fifty is a mid-sized grind: starting it in the activity phase rather than at 100% cleanup keeps it painless.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it completely and escape. Stage it somewhere with a clean exit — raise the stars in open ground, then break line of sight and hide until the search ends; the trophy needs the full cycle, stars earned together and heat fully lost together, in one run.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner while keeping your wanted level alive the whole time — if the stars drop to zero between shops, the chain breaks. Pick a cluster of shops on one street, keep a fast car outside each door, and move the moment each register is empty; momentum, not loot size, is what this trophy measures.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — a vehicle counts when you get in and drive it. Rich districts spawn the rare end of the catalogue, so make a habit of swapping into anything you have not driven before; five minutes of car-hopping in a wealthy area nets more new models than an hour of highway driving. The counter here tracks your running total.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop 5 enemies inside one Combat Focus activation. Do not burn the meter on the first pair of enemies you meet — save a full meter for a packed moment: a gang operation, a robbery gone loud, any doorway with five-plus hostiles. Line the shots up before you trigger it; the window is generous if the targets are already framed.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from its official description: the departure happens at VCIA, the airport the story visits for VCIA Takedown — the story visit is the one guaranteed window, so earn it there rather than assuming free-roam access.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — earn it during the story. While you are at VCIA (Vice City International Airport) for the VCIA Takedown mission, leave the airport in an unscheduled way: take an aircraft you were never cleared to take and get airborne. The story visit puts you on the airfield with planes in reach; if you finish the mission and leave normally, you may not get the same access again, which is why this guide flags it from its description.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Rhinos are the army's tanks, and they roll out at the top of a wanted level. Push your stars to maximum in open ground, let the Rhinos arrive, and engage them — heavy weapons or a commandeered Rhino of your own even the odds. It is one of the most-earned hidden trophies in Exophase's launch recording (1.57%), because a long police chase delivers it almost by accident.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store clean: in and out without being detected. Scout the store first, go in quiet, control the room without raising an alarm, and leave before attention arrives — a detection at any point voids the attempt, but attempts are free, so reset and refine the route until one run is spotless.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one — a vault only counts if you get away, so plan the exit before you crack it: vehicle staged, route rehearsed, heat managed. Vaults are the heavy end of the robbery set; warm up on shops and the armored truck first, then work the five banks one at a time.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the take. Hit the truck hard and fast to crack it open, grab the money, and be gone before the response escalates — like the bank vaults, the escape is part of the requirement, so stage your getaway car facing out before you strike.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — an area counts when you enter and reveal it. This completes almost by itself if you run the collection phase properly: card sets, meditation spots and WAiNK locations drag you into every corner of the state. If the counter stalls in the high 40s, the missing areas are usually offshore or mountain pockets no objective visits; sweep the map edges by boat and air.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Variety is the requirement — robbing the same gang twice does not advance the counter — so spread the hits across gang territories and note which colours you have already taken from. One clean robbery per gang; use the tracker counter to keep the set straight.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail at a spot with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to the beachfront bars on Ocean Beach, order the drink and take in the view — the trophy is the moment, not a challenge. An easy, pleasant detour to bank the first time you pass the beach.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Get into a vehicle inside a showroom and drive it out through the glass. Pick a car on the showroom floor, get behind the wheel and accelerate straight through the storefront — 'classic style' means the direct route, not the door. Any showroom works; expect a wanted level for the exit.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and follow through on your throw. Visit the alley, start a game and bowl — the trophy rides on taking the shot properly at this specific alley, so a bowling game anywhere else does not substitute. Pairs with Ten Pin if you fancy the alley's crowd afterwards.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from its official description: it is a one-off partnership moment ('a partnership with mass appeal'), the kind of scripted beat that plays once in the story — watch for it during partner missions rather than in free roam.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — a one-off partnership moment. The official description ('a partnership with mass appeal') points at a scripted beat with your partner rather than a repeatable free-roam action: stay alert during the story's partner missions, and when the pair of you draw a crowd, lean into the moment instead of rushing the objective. Keeping a manual save before partner set-pieces is the insurance if it passes you by.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from its official description: it counts choices made (PlayStation tracks the count to 500), and a choice once made cannot be unmade in the same playthrough — a manual save before a major story choice is the safety net.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE in spirit — this trophy counts the choices you make, and PlayStation tracks the count all the way to 500. Choices cannot be unmade inside one playthrough, so the discipline is simple: keep a rolling manual save before big story decisions, make your choices deliberately rather than by timeout, and the count climbs as the campaign and its side content present them. Reloading a pre-choice save lets you register the other branch's choice too.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable from its official description: 'second time's the charm' means the trophy needs a retry — succeed at something on the second attempt. A first-try success can close the window, so if a set-piece offers a retry, the retry is the trophy.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — this one rewards the retry, not the ace. Its description ('second time's the charm') tells you the shape: something must be attempted, failed or fallen short, and then succeeded on the second try. If you are the kind of player who nails set-pieces first time, this can slip past — when a story or activity beat offers you another attempt after a stumble, take it instead of reloading for a flawless run.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. Leonida hides an odd encounter out in its wilds — the trophy pops when you are present for the weird event rather than for anything you kill or collect. Explore off the roads at night, follow up anything the world does that looks staged-but-unexplained, and do not fast-travel past the state's quiet corners; this is the exploration trophy's stranger sibling.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a pedestrian down with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, strike someone with a melee attack as you pass. Ride or drive slowly past a target on a crowded pavement — too fast and the swing whiffs, too slow and it is just a punch. One clean connection is all it takes.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from the robbery economy — vaults, trucks and operations — so this trophy is the robbery phase's savings account: route every marked payout through your laundering contacts instead of spending it raw, and the quarter-million accumulates across the cleanup phases. The counter here tracks dollars laundered.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in total. It sounds like a grind and is not: weapons, armour, vehicle work, clothing and property-adjacent shopping all count, and a completion playthrough spends well past the threshold. If you are short late, the vehicle customisation shops burn money fastest.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. This is a money trophy wearing a property trophy's clothes: the garages unlock as the story opens the map, and the robbery and laundering income from phase 5 is what pays for them. Buy them as they appear rather than saving for a spree — each garage is also storage your vehicle collection will use.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Registration is done through the app when you are in a vehicle, so make it a habit: every new car you hop into for Whip It Good is a registration candidate too, and the two counters climb together. Ten is a small set — this should fall early in the collection phase.
